page.headline_chosen: I flipped my pillow to the cool side every night for years. Here's what finally stopped it.
page.byline: By Maya Chen, co-founder of Loftline. Loftline makes and sells the pillow in this story.

sections.text: For about six years, my nights went the same way. I'd fall asleep fine. Then sometime around 3am I'd wake up hot, my face pressed into a pillow that felt like it had been sitting in the sun. I'd flip it to find the cool side, fall back asleep, and wake up again an hour later to do it all over. If that sounds like your night, this page is for you. I'm going to tell you what I tried, what finally worked, and why, and I'll be straight about who it won't help.

Here's what I didn't understand back then. Your face and neck rest on the pillow for hours. Most pillows are a dense block of foam or fibre wrapped in cotton, and through the night they warm up to match you. So the pillow keeps getting warmer, and the only cool spot is the side you haven't been lying on. That's why the flip works for twenty minutes and then stops working. When I started reading our customers' reviews later, I found the same night described again and again: waking up hot, waking up sweaty, flipping the pillow over and over. I wasn't the only one.

I tried a lot before I made anything. A thin pillow, which ran cooler but left me with a stiff neck. A gel pillow that felt cold for the first few minutes and then warmed up like everything else. A fan pointed at the bed, which my partner hated. Sleeping with the window open in January. Each one fixed part of the problem and created another. The thin pillow taught me something useful, though: height matters as much as temperature. A pillow that's cool but the wrong height just swaps one bad morning for a different one.

In 2023 I started working on a pillow with two jobs: stay cooler for longer, and fit the person sleeping on it. The cooling had to come from the cover touching your skin, not from a gel layer buried inside, because the cover is what your face actually feels. And the fill had to be adjustable, because no single height suits a side sleeper, a back sleeper and a stomach sleeper. We tested covers for months. The one we kept uses a phase-change fabric, a material that absorbs heat as it warms, so it feels cool to the touch for longer than cotton does.

We sent the cover to an independent textile lab to check that it wasn't just a nice feeling. In their test, the cover surface measured 2.1°C cooler than a cotton pillowcase after 30 minutes of contact. That's the cool feel our reviewers describe when they roll over. Inside, the fill is shredded foam, and the cover unzips. If the pillow is too high for you, take a handful out until your neck sits level. The cover is machine washable at 40°C, so the sweat from all those hot nights doesn't stay in it.

We've sold 48,000 of these pillows since 2023, and buyers rate them 4.6 out of 5 across 1,240 verified reviews. The reviews I read most are the ones that describe my old nights. Dana R., who let us share her words, wrote: "I used to wake up at 3am soaked and flipping my pillow over and over. Now I sleep through most nights and the pillow still feels cool when I roll over." Not every review is like that. Some people find it too firm even with fill taken out, and a few don't notice much difference in temperature. That's why the next part matters.

The Loftline Cooling Pillow is $89, or $159 for two. You get 100 nights to sleep on it. If it doesn't help, send it back within those 100 nights for a full refund, and we pay the return shipping. I set it up that way because a pillow is impossible to judge in a shop. You only know after a few weeks of real nights.

Will it stay cool all night? The lab measured the cover cooler than cotton after 30 minutes; it isn't an air conditioner, and a very hot bedroom will still feel warm. What if it's the wrong height? Take fill out a handful at a time until your neck sits level. Does it go flat? Read the reviews on the product page, where buyers who've slept on it for months talk about exactly that. What if I don't like it? Return it within 100 nights for a full refund.
If you're tired of starting your nights over at 3am, see the pillow, the full reviews, and the single and two-pack options on the product page.
